Spec: warn on an `http://` or `ws://` URL to a non-loopback host and on a header value that looks like a literal credential. Code: insecureUrl (mcp-check.ts:62) checks only `http:`; no header-credential check exists (a `ws://example.com` server and an `Authorization: Bearer sk-...` header both give no finding). Add both warnings.

Spec: each result carries errors, warnings, notes and `gatingHooks` (module, pattern, hook, hasCatch). The plugin validator report (validate-run.ts ValidationFileResult, :55) has no gatingHooks and always empty notes; only the separate mod validator (src/mods/load/commands/validate.ts:39) emits gatingHooks, and its entries are plain strings, not the {path, message} of J17.15. One report shape should carry both.

Spec item 2: a line pasted with the placeholder `<owner>/<repo>` unchanged does not count, so the advice stays. Code: readmeInstallsPlugin (validate-advice.ts:27) counts any `--marketplace <word>`, so `/plugin install p --marketplace <owner>/<repo>` returns true and clears the advice (checked with bun -e). adviceNeedsSource exists but is not used by the counting. The implementation should change; the test covers only the generated line.

Note: ARCHIVE = /\.zip$/i (flags/plugins.ts:17) still compares the extension without regard to case, the reference-only behaviour the verification pass removed from the text; the spec is now silent, so this is not a divergence.
Bare mode skips hooks as a kind (customizations.ts:26), so hooks from --settings and from flag-loaded plugins do not run; flag-loaded plugins and --add-dir skills still load.

ADD_DIR_CONFIGURATION covers skills, commands, agents and the two settings keys; additionalDirectories is file access only. It also lists CLAUDE.md/CLAUDE.local.md behind CLAUDE_CODE_ADDITIONAL_DIRECTORIES_CLAUDE_MD, which the row does not mention but does not contradict.

Spec (fixed text): with -p the wait is MCP_TIMEOUT (default 30 s; shorter in a self-hosted environment), except a server with a cached tool list, which connects on first use. Code (flags/mcp.ts:24,67-73) has the 30 s default and MCP_TIMEOUT only: no self-hosted shortening and no cached-tool-list exception. Implementation should change (or report the environment fact through the flag context).

Core form in one client: missing entirely. Needed: form decision per root (§1.3 table, dual = Claude Code only); a core loader (plugin.json with core $schema, skills/ one level, mcp.json, hooks.json; ignore every Claude Code location and extensions); a core hook runner (exec form, one JSON object on stdin, cwd plugin root, exit 0 + one object or nothing, everything else a non-blocking failure, CC timeouts/caps); occurrence mapping of the five events and the cross-form combination rules (PreToolUse CC-first then core, decision precedence, one Stop continuation, handler order); core subprocess environment; core server registration under plugin:<name>:<server> with core §7.2 validation; settings/policy/permissions/skills by id. Size: large, roughly 1,500-2,500 lines plus tests, mostly new modules beside src/hooks, src/loading and src/settings; the hook engine needs a second handler kind and a combination step.

Event and result mapping: missing. Needed: per-event input builders (common fields, SessionStart/UserPromptSubmit/PreToolUse/PostToolUse/Stop fields) and result readers both ways, plus the tool profiles of §18.2.7 (shell, file.read with line-numbered text and binary pages, file.modify incl. NotebookEdit absolute path, WebFetch, WebSearch items, mcp). Size: medium, about 600-1,000 lines of pure tables and tests; shared by §18.1 and the §18.4 adapter.

Dual packages: the Claude Code half already behaves (a dual package validates as a plugin; J18.19 messages match). Missing: recognising the root core plugin.json so a dual package loads as Claude Code only and SHOULD be shown as also carrying a core manifest (§1.3.1), and a core validator for a core package (§18.1.5 item 6). Size: small, about 100-300 lines, most of it shared with the §18.1 form decision.

Conversion: missing; no converter exists. Needed: core-to-plugin and plugin-to-core converters (manifest copy, skill checks, MCP table with env bridging J18.18, reporting every loss with its path, no renaming, deterministic, dual output by default) and a hook adapter program translating inputs, results and exit statuses by §18.2. Size: large, about 1,000-1,500 lines plus the adapter runtime; it can be a separate entry point (it is a tool, not part of a session).
